messages:
maria: quick heads-up — exploring a different angle for SDK paging+retry ergonomics. think of it as: transport advertises capabilities, SDK negotiates a minimal set, and pagination/shim behavior is derived from that.
aj: hmm — capability-driven transports? can you give an example?
maria: e.g., transport can expose: streaming, resumable-pages, idempotent-reqs, server-cursors. SDK uses those flags to pick: async iterator vs stream vs page-based retry logic.
kevin: I like the idea. avoids baking assumptions into the SDK. what about older runtimes (fetch-only browsers)?
sophia: fallback path: if resumable-pages missing -> SDK falls back to client-side cursor + page-level retry (more conservative). will need shims for TS and Python to keep API parity.
aj: main risk is cognitive load for app devs. they expect one behavior. how do we make it nondisruptive?
maria: default: SDK chooses the most resilient semantics (no surprises). advanced callers can opt-in to lower-latency behaviors via a small opt-in config: {"transportHints": ["streaming","resumable-pages"]}.
kevin: implementation detail question: how do we represent resume tokens so they’re cross-language safe? base64 opaque blob?
sophia: propose compact resume token model: base64 of JSON-LD-like blob: {v:1, model: "gpt-*", cursor: "...", checksum: "..."}. but keep transport header hint: x-rw-resume-cap=fingerprint to avoid huge payloads.
aj: checksum to detect incompatible resume semantics — good. what about security/PII concerns? tokens must not leak prompt content.
maria: tokens should be server-generated opaque handles by default; if server returns full state then we require flag/responsibility on server side. SDK docs must warn against storing raw state.
kevin: retry semantics: we discussed page-level retries vs per-record retries historically. capability-driven approach lets transport tell us if it supports "at-least-once-resume" vs "exactly-once".
sophia: exact-once is expensive; most transports will advertise at-least-once + idempotency-key support. SDK can then: 1) use idempotency keys for mutations, 2) dedupe at consumer layer for read streams if needed.
aj: ergonomics across languages: Python async iterator, TS async iterable/ReadableStream, Go chan + context. we need a single mental model: "continuable iteration" with small language adapters.
maria: agreed. surface: iterator that yields items and exposes .resume_token on the iterator object (or return [item, resume_token] for languages that prefer value types).
kevin: code sketch (TS):
```ts
for await (const chunk of client.listThings({limit: 100, transportHints: ['resumable-pages']})) {
  // chunk.items
  // client can call .resume(token) later
}
```
kevin: Python sketch:
```py
async for chunk in client.list_things(limit=100, transport_hints=['resumable-pages']):
    pass
# iterator.resume_token attribute available on the iterator object
```
sophia: Go sketch:
```go
it := client.ListThings(ctx, opts)
for it.Next() {
  item := it.Item()
}
if tok := it.ResumeToken(); tok != "" {
  // persist for later
}
```
aj: one contentious bit: should resume tokens be first-class return values from the API (part of response body) or only available on iterator object?
maria: prefer iterator-exposed token to avoid polluting the main response schema for simple callers. servers can still include token in body for advanced flows.
kevin: what about retries across pagination boundary? if a page fails midway, we retry at page granularity using resume token from previous successful page. that avoids re-fetching entire sequence but is conservative.
sophia: agree. also propose optional "client-side partial-merge" hook: server may return partial_progress marker so client can merge incremental items. opt-in via capability.
aj: testing strategy? need cross-lang contract tests around capability negotiation, token formats, and backoff.
maria: plan: add transport capability matrix fixture in the e2e harness. run permutations: http1 (no streaming, resumable-pages), http2 (streaming, resumable-pages), quic (streaming, resumable-pages, lower-latency), mock-bad (no-resume).
kevin: CI-bot: will add matrix lanes and a lightweight contract test that asserts: resume_token roundtrips, token checksum mismatch yields clear error, client falls back on missing capabilities.
ci-bot: CI note — created job: sdk-transport-cap-matrix with 6 permutations; triggers on eng-platform/* and sdk/* PRs. :robot_face:
maria: next steps: 1) draft a small RFC (one pager) with examples (TS/Py/Go), capability enum, and migration path; 2) add transport hint field to SDK request options; 3) implement negotiation shim in the runtime HTTP client.
aj: timeline?
maria: RFC this week, prototype in TS next sprint, Python + Go follow-on. will post RFC in #eng-platform once ready. feedback?
kevin: lgtm overall. just make sure docs call out security and long-term wire stability.
sophia: +1. also add a short cookbook entry for "fast streaming vs resumable safe" choices.
aj: thanks, team. I'll help with the TS prototype.
maria: thanks — will ping when RFC is up. :sparkles:
